messages:
maya (Finance): Heads-up — got today's preliminary invoice and usage looks ~18% higher than our internal token counts for March 19-21. Suspect the backfill that ran last night double-counted embeddings. Can someone from infra confirm?

sam (Billing): ugh. Do we have a diff file or a query we can run to reconcile billable vs counted tokens? I want to know if this is an invoice credit or internal accounting adjustment.

li (Eng Infra): Looking into it now. We had a logging outage on 2026-03-20 03:10-03:45 UTC and we ran a backfill job afterwards. Paging the metering service logs. @oliver any recent changes to the dedupe job?

oliver (Platform): No code changes to dedupe in the last 7 days. But we bumped the KV cache TTL which might have affected prefix caching and the backfill job's idempotency check. Not sure.

metering-bot: INFO 2026-03-21T02:12:11Z - backfill/ingest started (job_id=bf-20260320-21). Processed shards: 12/12.

li (Eng Infra): Found suspicious pattern in backfill logs: same client_request_id appears twice in a short window. Possible duplicate ingestion. Snippet: ```sql
SELECT client_request_id, count(*) FROM metering_events
WHERE event_time BETWEEN '2026-03-19' AND '2026-03-22'
GROUP BY client_request_id
HAVING count(*) > 1
LIMIT 10;```

rachel (Ops): If client_request_id duplicates caused double billing of tokens, we need to decide: 1) ask vendor for invoice credit, 2) adjust our internal reported usage and send corrected invoice to customer, or 3) both. Recommendation: prepare a rollback diff and then open a vendor ticket.

sam (Billing): Can we compute a conservative estimate of over-billed tokens so we can pre-authorize a credit? Even ballpark is fine.

li (Eng Infra): Running a quick aggregation now. Early numbers: ~2.1M extra tokens from embeddings and ~350k generation tokens across affected window. That's ~18% of the billed units on that invoice. I'll export CSV to /tmp/billing-backfill-diff.csv and share.

maya (Finance): Thanks. Can you also include rate-limit vs billable lookups? One question the customer raised: were tokens suppressed by 429s counted as billable? We need to show that rate-limited requests were not double-billed.

oliver (Platform): Rate-limits are applied at the gateway; failed requests with 4xx are not forwarded to metering by design. But backfill code reads raw event logs and didn't check status_code for a short period due to a missing field mapping. Fix is trivial.

alex (Head of Finance): Plan: li to produce CSV + SQL diff; sam to draft vendor ticket and request preliminary credit for ~18%; maya to prepare customer-facing explanation and offer a one-off credit if customer experienced overage. Approval: Alex OKs up to $5k immediate credit, beyond that requires exec sign-off.

sam (Billing): Drafted ticket to vendor with attached CSV + query results. Subject: "Potential duplicate ingestion during backfill — request invoice review". Included invoice ID and sample event ids. Sending now. :email:

maya (Finance): I'll prep a short note for affected customers summarizing cause (backfill duplicates), what we fixed, and the remediation timeline. Will propose automated credit for all impacted accounts once vetting is done.

li (Eng Infra): Patch merged to backfill idempotency check. Running a dry re-run on a small shard to validate de-dup logic. ETA for full re-run: 3 hours. Will update CSV after re-run.

oliver (Platform): Also adding a monitoring alert to detect >0.5% discrepancy between realtime-metering and backfill-aggregates over a rolling 24h window.

meyering (Note: added as a quick follow-up): Is there an action item for finance org to hold approval until updated CSV?

maya (Finance): Yes — hold external credits until li confirms corrected numbers. Internal memo ready to managers.

sam (Billing): Vendor responded asking for sample logs and the corrected counts. They said credits typically take 5-7 business days. I've asked for interim invoice hold.

li (Eng Infra): Re-run finished. New numbers: extra tokens now ~1.9M total (embeddings reduced after de-dupe). CSV updated and uploaded to /tmp/billing-backfill-final.csv.

maya (Finance): Great. Sam, proceed to request provisional credit for $3.8k (estimate). Alex, please confirm if that's within the $5k pre-approved.

alex (Head of Finance): Confirmed. Approve provisional credit request up to $5k. If vendor offers less, we'll reconcile internally. Please cc me on the final vendor resolution.

rachel (Ops): Closing loop: deploy notes added to postmortem, added runbook step to validate status_code field in ingestion for backfills.

maya (Finance): Thanks team. I'll schedule a short sync tomorrow to finalize customer comms and postmortem. :calendar:
